question: Where was the halo effect first measured, and what gave it away?
answer: In army officers' ratings of their own soldiers, published in 1920. Edward Thorndike found that marks for physique, intellect, leadership and character moved together far more than such different traits could; the correlations, he wrote, were too high and too even. A soldier who stood well also got judged clever.
move: When every score on a sheet agrees, suspect one impression wrote them all.
reference: Thorndike, A constant error in psychological ratings, Journal of Applied Psychology, 1920
